[College group, 9:14 pm]
Sameer: [reel: rooftop infinity pool, Dubai skyline] good times 🥂
Tushar: bhai owns half of Gurgaon now, look at this lifestyle
Sameer: expanding soon boys, watch this space 😎
---
[DM, 11:52 pm]
Sameer: Faisal, quick thing. asking for a friend — any openings in your company? operations or general management side. 15-18 LPA bracket is fine.
Sameer: he's looking to move this month itself. solid guy, ran his own setup for years.
Sameer: and yaar don't bring this up in the group, he's private about it.
Faisal: arre sure sure, I'll check with HR on Monday 👍
---
[College group, next day, 1:30 pm]
Faisal: reunion venue sorted then — Sameer bhai will sponsor, business is booming 😂
Tushar: 😂😂 gym king
Sameer: 👍
---
[DM, three days later]
Faisal: hey, HR asked for the friend's CV, can you send?
Faisal: hello? bhai?

---
1. Who is the "friend" in Sameer's DM and how do you know? What is the third-person framing doing for Sameer — why this exact costume?
2. Trace what Faisal's group message on the next day did to Sameer. Why did the DM go silent — connect the thumbs-up, the joke, and the three-day silence.
3. Write the DM Faisal should send now, exactly as he should send it, that gets Sameer real help without ever making him admit anything.

**1. The "friend" is Sameer himself.**

The evidence is in the mismatch between the two registers. In the group, Sameer posts a Dubai rooftop reel and claims he's "expanding soon." Minutes later, in the DM, "a friend" is job-hunting, needs to move *this month*, and — the tell — is "private about it," with an explicit instruction not to mention it in the group. A real friend's job search wouldn't need secrecy from a college group; only *Sameer's* would. The 15–18 LPA bracket and "ran his own setup for years" also fit Sameer exactly: someone whose business likely collapsed or is failing ("expanding soon" is the cover story), who needs employment but can't be seen needing it.

The third-person framing is emotional armor. It lets Sameer ask for help without asking — if Faisal says no, no real rejection occurred; if word leaks, it's "my friend," not him. It preserves the persona the group knows (the successful one, the sponsor) while getting the actual need met. He's outsourcing his humiliation to a fictional character.

**2. Faisal's group message cornered him.**

By joking publicly that "business is booming" and that Sameer would sponsor the reunion, Faisal — innocently, right after agreeing to help — reinforced the exact myth Sameer is trapped inside. Now helping Sameer means colluding in the lie; refusing means contradicting the booming-business narrative. Every path forces Sameer to either perform success further (sponsor, pay up) or let the mask slip.

So the thumbs-up 👍 is not agreement — it's damage control. Sameer can't explain why sponsorship is suddenly awkward without unraveling everything, so he gives the cheapest acknowledgment possible and exits. Then the DM goes silent because the request has become radioactive: HR wants a CV, which means producing documents, a real name, a real person — and the "friend" doesn't exist. Answering means confessing; not answering preserves the fiction at the cost of the job. Three days of silence is Sameer choosing the mask over the rescue.

**3. The DM Faisal should send now:**

> "Bhai, small update. HR said they're doing a batch of ops/GM hires this quarter, so instead of one CV they want a shortlist of 3-4 profiles — makes it look like proper volume on their side. So send me your friend's details whenever, zero rush, he'll just be one of a few names.
>
> Also completely unrelated — I'm putting together the reunion budget and I'd rather keep sponsorships flexible, nothing locked yet. Don't let Tushar fix you into anything 😂
>
> And yaar, whatever happens with this stays between us like always. Even if nothing works out, nobody hears a thing from my side."

Why this works: the "batch hiring" lie removes the CV bottleneck — Sameer can stall or send minimal info without the "friend" needing to materialize fully, and there's no single spotlight on him. The reunion line quietly dissolves the sponsorship trap Faisal himself created, giving Sameer an exit that costs him nothing. And the closing promise guarantees the secret stays safe even in total failure — removing the exact fear (exposure) that caused the silence. Sameer never has to admit anything; he only has to reply.
